chunks: Praise of God: We praise Him for whatever He takes or gives, and for whatever He tests and tries us with,
The Hidden One is aware of every secret, the Present One is aware of every inner state, the All-Knowing of what the breasts conceal, and what the eyes betray.

And we bear witness that there is no god but He, and that Muhammad is His noble one and His messenger, a testimony in which the secret matches the public declaration, and the heart matches the tongue.

key_terms.السَّرِيرَة: Inner state or secret of the heart
key_terms.الْبَاطِنُ: The Hidden/Inner One, referring to God's awareness of secrets

ai.seo_question: What does this supplication say about God's knowledge of hidden secrets?
ai.summary: This passage, often cited as the opening of the famous 'Sermon of the Death of the Prophet' or general supplications in Nahj al-Balagha, reflects the Shia emphasis onanistic tradition of linking divine omniscience (Ilm) with the inner purity of the heart. It underscores the concept of 'Mu'awana' (divine assistance) where the external declaration of Shahadah aligns perfectly with internal conviction, a key theme in Shia spiritual psychology. The text serves as a bridge between the cosmic attributes of Allah and the human experience of faith, highlighting that true belief is known to God even before it is spoken.

en.sayed-ali-raza: We praise Him for whatever He takes or gives or whatever He inflicts on us or tries us with.
He is aware of all that is hidden and He sees all that is concealed. He knows all that breasts contain or eyes hide.

We render evidence that there is no god except He and that Muḥammad — peace be upon him and his progeny — has been chosen by Him and deputed by Him — evidence tendered both secretly and openly, by heart and by tongue.
